body.title: My participation in the Reflection Hunters Contest - #SMARP round #259: Spring 2026 postcards [Eng/Esp]
body.body: >\n\nHappy Saturday [Shadow Hunters](https://ecency.com/created/hive-179017) community! It's not always possible to see the reflection in the photo I'm showing you for this #SMARP [round 259](https://ecency.com/hive-179017/@olgavita/reflection-hunters-contest-smarp-show-8945d93e77e62), and yes, you might think this is just a swimming pool filled with water that hasn't been changed in weeks. But the truth is, this is the remnant of what was meant to be a swimming pool, but never was. This sort of summer house was never finished in the 1950s and was taken over by the University during those years of dictatorship and converted into a research center. Since then, that pool has been empty, containing only enough water to keep our pet caiban, \

hydrated. However, in 2024, something unusual happened: the water valves broke, flooding the school's green spaces, including the pool! This allowed us to witness something unprecedented: the pool completely full, and yes, our greatest fear materialized—Babushka almost climbing out of the pool! Well, that was almost two years ago! Due to the crisis that has now escalated into a military intervention in Venezuela, many maintenance services at the school have ceased, and, well, the inevitable happened: the pool flooded again because the replacement pipe that had been installed previously broke. The good news was that the floodwaters didn't rise above the pool's surface, so Babushka couldn't get out. This allowed us to work more calmly and begin the process of dredging the pool. The interesting thing is that I was one of the first to arrive at the institute and had the unique opportunity to photograph the pool and the water feature that was created, which I wanted to share with you for this week's SMARP.
![photo_1_2026-02-20_23-15-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/AKKSZJTaDzcX6H1cc4oTcRHDvRrzA9U8XzdbGSznGbxzkLro2TMBUgZNDFyh5Rv.jpg) --- ![photo_5_2026-02-20_23-15-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tmMvv3VCmjXVryJ5ZwgLeesMUJ8hRuZyJVVE7eBRyMXGKDRe1ohJemb1gn7Aj1L6Z55.jpg)

> The water leak wasn't too severe because when we left last weekend, none of the workers came back to check on the slight break in the main pipe. So, when I arrived, what I saw was this partial reflecting pool because over the weekend, duckweed, a type of aquatic plant that tends to eutrophicate lakes and ponds, had grown. This prevented a wider, clearer reflection, but since it formed naturally, I think it adds a certain charm to the image.
![photo_4_2026-02-20_23-15-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23wC7wjLbNYhoAh7hBZkgySTrNiHMhPTsmc38qo9vsVBC19yginGLBWownN8sL5vUtiFk.jpg)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRvWxqnFqswK34rLXwwDzLFHimD2xstYf7ZmmjmX39TA7DFGfV3AbTDuBxHmK6AMydA.png)

> A short time later, the university workers arrived, and with the help of the town hall, they managed to dredge the pool. Our pet was in the deepest part, where most of the sediment and mud had settled. It was covered in mud, but it seemed happy; I suppose it was somehow mimicking its state in the wild. Ultimately, although it was a mishap that was quickly resolved, it gave us these wonderful reflections, which I hope you like. See you at the next SMARP, friends. Happy weekend! Best regards!
--- # Versión Español ---
![photo_2_2026-02-20_23-15-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23uFPUEw9mkdt1g96hLYisxe9aPT6eY5gRnSerJvjFBtCZwHKqHfGGtc7YQCFmtrxvJz1.jpg)

>\n\nFeliz sábado comunidad de [Shadow Hunters](https://ecency.com/created/hive-179017)!  No siempre es posible comtemplar el reflejo generado en la fotografía que te estoy mostrando para este #SMARP [round 259](https://ecency.com/hive-179017/@olgavita/reflection-hunters-contest-smarp-show-8945d93e77e62), y si, puedes pensar que esta es una simple piscina llena de agua con semanas sin haber sido cambiada en semanas. Pero la realidad es que este es el vestigio de lo que eventualmente sería una piscina y nunca llegó a serlo porque originalmente esta especie de casa de veraneo nunca se terminó de construir en los años cincuenta y fue tomado por la Universidad en aquellos años de dictadura y reconvertido en un centro de investigación. Desde entonces esa piscina ha estado vacía con una cantidad de agua basal para mantener el caiban que tenemos de mascota, \

hidratada. Sin embargo desde el 2024 sucedió algo singular las llaves de paso de agua se rompieron inundando los espacios verdes del instituto, incluyendo la piscina! Esto nos permitió ver un evento nunca antes visto, ver la piscina completamente llena y si, nuestro mayor temor se materializó, ver a babushka casi salir de la piscina! Bueno, eso fue hace casi ya 2 años! Debido a la crisis que ahora ha derivado en una agresión militar en Venezuela, muchos de los servicios de mantenimiento en el instituto han cesado y bueno, paso lo inevitable, se volvió a inundar las piscina por la rotura del tubo de repuesto que se había colocado anteriormente. Lo bueno fue que la inundación no sobrepasó la piscina asi que babushka no pudo salir de la piscina, eso nos permitió trabajar más tranquilos y comenzar el proceso de dragado de la piscina. Lo interesante es que yo fui de los primeros en llegar al instituto y tuve la oportunidad única de fotografíar la piscina y el espejo de agua que se genero y que he querido traerte para el SMARP de esta semana.
![photo_1_2026-02-20_23-15-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/AKKSZJTaDzcX6H1cc4oTcRHDvRrzA9U8XzdbGSznGbxzkLro2TMBUgZNDFyh5Rv.jpg) --- ![photo_5_2026-02-20_23-15-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tmMvv3VCmjXVryJ5ZwgLeesMUJ8hRuZyJVVE7eBRyMXGKDRe1ohJemb1gn7Aj1L6Z55.jpg)

> El bote de agua no fue tan severo ya que cuando nos fuimos el fin de semana pasado, nadie de los obreros volvió para darse cuenta que había una ligera rotura de la tubería principal. Entonces, cuando llegué lo que vi fue este espejo de agua parcial porque a lo largo del fin de semana había crecido lemna una especie de planta acuática que tiende a eutrificar lagos y pozos de agua, eso impidió un reflejo más amplio y limpio de la imagen, pero al ser algo que se formó naturalmente, creo que le da algo de encanto a la imagen.
![photo_4_2026-02-20_23-15-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23wC7wjLbNYhoAh7hBZkgySTrNiHMhPTsmc38qo9vsVBC19yginGLBWownN8sL5vUtiFk.jpg)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRvWxqnFqswK34rLXwwDzLFHimD2xstYf7ZmmjmX39TA7DFGfV3AbTDuBxHmK6AMydA.png)

> Poco tiempo después llegaron los obreros de la universidad y con la ayuda de la alcaldía del municipio lograron dragar la piscina, nuestra mascota se encontraba en la parte más profunda donde había caído la mayor parte del sedimento y lodo, estaba toda llena de barro pero parecía estar feliz, supongo que de alguna manera emulaba su estado en la naturaleza salvaje. En ultima instancia aunque fue un percance que se logro solucionar rápidamente, nos regaló estos maravillosos reflejos que espero les gusten. Nos vemos en el próximo SMARP amigos. Feliz fin de semana. Saludos!
![ecency_spring_banner2025_6.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/243fzw92qU1TYGxoTAtzTQ2BAwNmSPvZhpG2EXsZmzEA3t3KtSL88hxURV3sy74U2iX9R.gif) ![ecency_spring_banner2025_10 II.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/245TSwLsaP8B4DpGdfKu1AnCcDxAEpYqNkHS7CjSaz767Qfd9utXB3W5uvaPhkJgcjhys.gif)

> The images for this post were taken from my Redmi 9c cell phone. The translation was done with the [Deepl](https://www.deepl.com/es/translator) translate. > Las imágenes para este post fueron tomadas en mi móvil Redmi 9c. La traducción fue realizada con [Deepl](https://www.deepl.com/es/translator) translate.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tb64j1ot2GsUmkVQ3tCfAdWNkvhWxHFJXLVcLYcXESENCc8opqYUnZNCT9hrYp5s3Kn.png) # Follow me on Hive!

body.title: Why Consulting a Pediatrician Is Important for Your Child’s Health
body.body:
Assalamu Alaikum,
Today, I want to share why it is sometimes very necessary to consult a specialist when it comes to your child’s health. 

Recently, I was thinking about how many parents today do not bother to visit a pediatrician for their child.

 Instead, they go to a general doctor to treat whatever illness their child is going through.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcWvKKSViRuQu63JTmSTfjRN5ZAAoqWJ4oygC3F7njoXY/image.png)

<a href=\

>Source Now, this is not completely wrong. However, when you consult a specialist, such as a pediatrician, they usually provide more appropriate treatment for children. For example, whenever I visit my pediatrician, I rarely see him prescribing antibiotics to my son. Most of the time, he simply asks us to monitor the situation, whether it is a fever or a cold. He only prescribes antibiotics when it is truly necessary. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNnFqw6SDMCj7nse1CY5FUxAbHLChqnZymGpkY6d4Koif/image.png)

>Source On the other hand, when you visit a general doctor who mainly treats adults, they may prescribe antibiotics from the very first day. While this might help your child recover quickly, the unseen and concerning part is that your child’s body does not get the chance to learn how to fight infections naturally. Childhood is a time of learning, not only mentally and physically in the outside world but also internally within the body. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfVvcgGavppSboq279VKsYAvLHBMrQH9umrrSnsiJDEXA/image.png)

>Source If antibiotics are given too frequently, the child’s body may become dependent on medication and may not build strong natural immunity. Over time, the child might rely on medicines whenever they experience similar symptoms. It is better to allow the child’s immune system to fight mild illnesses when possible and provide proper treatment at the right time. This helps ensure better health in the long run. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfYyV4SJDUPVmqxjksGCDTpVAv5ntzCT3x9br9bGdgr5b/image.png)

>Source Pediatricians are specialists. They spend years studying and researching child psychology, child growth, and childhood diseases. That is why they are called child specialists. Now, it is up to you to decide whether you want your child to be treated by a general doctor who may prescribe strong antibiotics immediately, or by a pediatrician who focuses on giving the right treatment at the right time, even if it takes a little longer for your child to recover. body.title: Relato: Ruidos a las cuatro de la mañana
body.body: ![Hive Banners 2026 (20).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vickaboleyn/48Fi7gMMCn1qHnpgAnZnjt63MnPBGhJ7KbFZ8bw4gc1yLrVsMcicZw3hmaSLZndSgn.png) **Imagen editada con Canva. Fuente de la imagen: [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/foto-de-primer-plano-de-hojas-verdes-3178786/)**

> Cuatro de la mañana. La luz del cuarto estaba encendida porque la habitación suele tener humedad durante el invierno tropical. Entre sueños, Alfonsina escuchó los golpes en la ventana. Pisadas tenues en la tierra.

Pensó que eran sueños o alucinaciones, porque los primeros golpes los escuché en medio del mundo onírico, pero los dos últimos los escuchó después de ir al baño, como si estuvieran lanzando piedras, a juzgar por la distancia de tiempo entre ruido y ruido.

O serán tres, con un sonido parecido más a los intentos de un ave queriendo entrar. ¿O sería un gato?

Negó con la cabeza. No. No era un animal.

Quizás sea un mal aire, algún mal espíritu o un fantasma travieso. No quería ni averiguarlo. Por eso no se levantó para acercarse a la ventana.

Optó por buscar en el Internet el Salmo 91, el de la protección divina. Lo rezó un par de veces con fervor, persignándose, enfocándose en el refugio del Altísimo, tratando de calmar su sobresalto.

De repente escuchó el ronquido de su hermano, quien dormía en el lado contiguo. Dichoso él, se dijo, quien no escucha nada, quien tiene el sueño tan profundo como el océano.

Miró la hora. 4:33 de la mañana. El ruido cesó, o eso creo. Solo Dios sabrá qué pasó.

Escuchó de repente que el portón del patio se abre. Su tía lo abrió por los perros, así que aprovechó levantarse y salir de su habitación para dirigirse a la planta baja.

Le narró a su tía lo sucedido mientras salíamos al patio cob la luz de mi teléfono encendida. Su tía comentó que escuchó pisadas en el techo. Alfonsina acechó con cierta rapidez, buscando al menos una huella. Los perros solo se enfocaron en ir al baño. Entraron a la casa, regresando cada quien a su cuarto.

Alfoinsina lanzó un suspiro apenas cerró la puerta. Su corazón estaba un poco acelerado ante tanto susto.

Tomó su teléfono y miró la hora. Cinco de la mañana. En una hora más el sol acecharía en el horizonte.

Apagó la luz, se acostó y cerró los ojos, perdiéndose en el mundo de los sueños.

body.title: Television Review: D.O.C. (Lost, S3X18, 2007)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/fSi3tZn6hVXFfWrZhDwPD4Z1d6I.jpg)

**D.O.C. (S03E18)**

Airdate: 25 April 2007

Written by: Edward Kitisis & Adam Horowitz
Directed by: Frederick E. O.  Toye

Running Time: 43 minutes



By the middle of Season 3, the collective consciousness of the Lost audience was in a state of complex frustration. While few could deny that the show possessed a unique ability to weave intricate narratives and evoke deep emotional responses, the very strengths that had once made it revolutionary were beginning to feel repetitive. The narrative formula, which had worked wonders in the first two seasons, was starting to feel like a rigid constraint rather than a flexible tool. Episodes that would have been hailed as masterpieces only a few months prior were now viewed with a critical eye, their slow pacing and adherence to established structures becoming increasingly apparent. It was within this context that the episode *D.O.C.* aired, serving as a very telling example of this phenomenon—a showcase of solid production values that nonetheless highlighted the show's struggle to evolve beyond its own conventions.

The title of the episode, \

a detail that is presented as a crucial piece of information, ostensibly intended to give away the ultimate fate of one of the show's major characters. This character is Sun, who is visibly pregnant and radiating a blissful happiness about it. However, as the narrative has painstakingly established over previous episodes, all women who become pregnant on the Island subsequently die, with the sole exception of those who, like Claire, became pregnant before their arrival. This established lore casts a long shadow over Sun's joy, creating a dramatic irony that the audience is desperate to see resolved, even if the resolution is tragic.

Sun remains blissfully unaware of the ticking clock until she is visited by Juliet, a character who serves as the Others' mole within the Losties camp and a scientist by trade. Juliet wants to ascertain the truth about Sun's condition and her ultimate fate. She brings Sun to the Staff Station, a location that features a secret compartment containing still-functioning equipment, including ultrasound monitors. At this point, Sun, having been told that Jin is sterile, believes that the child she is carrying was conceived during her extramarital affair with Jae. Consequently, she assumes that she and the baby are safe. Juliet performs a test and shows Sun an image of her unborn child, but her palpable delight is soon crushed by a devastating truth. The fetus is too young to have been conceived before the crash; therefore, Sun had conceived her baby on the Island, and Jin is the father. It appears that Jin's sterility, like other people's medical conditions on the Island, has been miraculously cured. Yet, this revelation means a death sentence for Sun, as she is told she has only two months to live. Juliet afterwards records her report to Ben, adding a personal note that she hates him.

The flashback sequences deal with Sun, and in some ways, they put her relationship with Jin in a different light, though they unfortunately reiterate what the audience already knew. The flashback is set immediately after their wedding when a mysterious woman approaches on the street and demands 100,000 US dollars in exchange for silence about Jin's mother being a prostitute—an unimaginable scandal if made public to Mr. Paik. Mr. Paik catches his daughter with the money and decides to keep quiet about it in exchange for asking his son-in-law to do some unspecified \

to him personally. Sun later meets Mr. Kwon, who confirms the woman's story, claiming that he raised Jin by himself and he isn't sure whether he was his biological son, but he treated him as such. Sun later pays the woman, who reveals herself to be Jin's mother, but also threatens her life if she dares to ask for money ever again. While this backstory adds texture to Sun's desperation to keep her marriage, it does not offer anything startlingly new.

The side storyline in the episode actually advances the general plot and deals with the mysterious female parachutist that Desmond, Jin, Charlie, and Hurley have discovered in the jungle. It turns out that she is hurt very badly and needs immediate medical attention. While the group contemplates whether to bring her to the beach or bring Jack to tend her wounds, Hurley, by accidentally shooting a flare from the gun, forces the issue. Now everyone, including the Others, could find their location. Mikhail suddenly appears from the jungle, apparently having survived the sonic barrier. He gets captured and, in exchange for his freedom, offers his expertise as a former Soviet Army field medic to help the woman. His efforts are successful, and he is reluctantly released. When the woman wakes up and is told by Hurley that she is among the survivors of Oceanic Flight 815, she acts with dismay, claiming that the plane was found and that there weren't any survivors.

Written by Edward Kitsis and Adam Horowitz, the episode is well-directed by Frederick E. O. Toye and features solid acting, but, for the most part, it doesn't add anything particularly new or anything the audience haven't been able to figure out beforehand. The pregnancy subplot had only two avenues—Sun carrying Jae's baby and living, or Sun carrying Jin's baby and dying—and the script opts for the latter, adding extra melodrama and plot complications to be resolved in the next couple of episodes or seasons. Even Sun's flashback doesn't add anything new, since the audience already knew about her husband's modest background being the source of possible shame and embarrassment for her rich father and family. It felt like padding to fill the runtime.

The only interesting addition is the action choreography, specifically when Jin delivers a roundhouse kick while overpowering Mikhail, establishing that character's apparent skill with martial arts. This moment provides a brief respite from the slow pacing but feels somewhat isolated in an episode otherwise focused on dialogue and exposition.

And then comes the major twist at the end that was supposed to add weeks or months of fan speculations and watercooler discussions in Spring of 2007. The parachutist claims that Oceanic Flight 815 was found and that all survivors are dead. If this is the truth, then the Island could be some sort of mystic purgatory. Alternatively, the whole electromagnetic business with the Swan Station could have created two versions of the doomed plane or parallel universes. Or, the female parachutist is simply lying. There were so many questions raised by this cliffhanger, but by that time, fans of Lost had grown accustomed to the pattern that answers delivered would often be disappointing or dragged out far longer than anticipated.



RATING: 6/10 (++)

body.body:
Ayer se jugó la primera jornada en las ligas de la Toronja y el Cactus. Cerró, de éste modo, la larga espera por el béisbol. Y en el site de MLB.com, nos dimos cuenta que -al menos para Venezuela- se transmitirían partidos gratis por MLB.tv. Así las cosas, no pudimos dejar pasar la oportunidad de ver algunos de los primeros partidos y nos decantamos por el que se realizaría en el Salt River Field, en Scottsdale, AZ; entre los DiamondBacks de Arizona y los Rockies de Colorado. Sin grandes nombres de por medio, chequeamos las alineaciones de cada escuadra en tres de los siete juegos difundidos de manera gratuita, con el fin de mirar aquel desafío donde peloteros venezolanos jugarían. Por los Rockies, abriría el venezolano Antonio Senzatela, quien forma parte de la rotación de la vinotinto que jugará el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol. En la receptoría de los Backs, estaría recibiendo los envíos Gabriel Moreno, titular de la posición en Phoenix. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     Yesterday marked the first day of play in the Grapefruit and Cactus Leagues, thus ending the long wait for baseball. And on MLB.com, we realized that—at least for Venezuela—games would be streamed for free on MLB.tv. So, we couldn't pass up the opportunity to watch some of the first games and chose the one being played at Salt River Field in Scottsdale, AZ, between the Arizona Diamondbacks and the Colorado Rockies. Without any big names involved, we checked the lineups for each team in three of the seven free-to-air games, hoping to find the one where Venezuelan players would be on the field. For the Rockies, Venezuelan Antonio Senzatela, part of the Venezuelan national team's rotation for the World Baseball Classic, would start. Behind the plate for the Diamondbacks, Gabriel Moreno, the starting catcher for Phoenix, would be catching the pitches.

---
![Senzatela.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23uFRXngGYtTsF6FUZrL7sUZNmanqHgzjcT8RBWmiT9vsBZSeKjYoio4kTLZwmv7TmP3d.jpg) Screenshot from [Vídeo](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/d-backs-vs-rockies/2026/02/20/831959/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
#
     Transcurría el cierre del primer episodio y Gabriel no esperó mucho para usar los desafíos ABS, al solicitar la revisión del tercer envío a la goma cantado como \
y resultando en el cambio de la apreciación por \

. Hay algo que es cierto como un sol, usted puede engañar a quien sea, pero cuando está delante de la cámara, no puede esconder sus emociones. El umpire se mostró contrariado y eso se notó en la cámara, tanto, que se puso de espaldas a la goma. En la imagen siguiente, se ve cuando Moreno se lleva la mano al casco y lo golpea, como señal de pedir el desafío. Lo bueno del caso es que tuvo razón, el resultado fue casi instantáneo y el juego no se vio comprometido en tiempo. No sólo tuvo la razón, es que no se contuvo en seguir usando el sistema varias veces, equivocándose una sola vez cuando una pelota cantada bola si estaba fuera por dos centímetros (es muy precisa la medición del seguimiento del pitcheo mediante cámara lenta). #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

      As the first inning drew to a close, Gabriel didn't wait long to use the ABS challenge, requesting a review of the third pitch called a ball, which resulted in the call being changed to a strike. One thing is certain: you can fool anyone, but when you're on camera, you can't hide your emotions. The umpire was visibly upset, and it showed on camera; he even turned his back to home plate. In the next image, you can see Moreno put his hand to his helmet and tap it, signaling his intention to challenge the pitch. The good news is that he was right; the result was almost instantaneous, and the game wasn't delayed. Not only was he right, but he didn't hesitate to use the system several more times, only making one mistake when a pitch called a ball was actually two centimeters out (the slow-motion pitch tracking is very precise).

---

![Moreno.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23wMcogfRmY8N8z3j2PjuyZg3VrSknR7xHsdcvgQPtCVeJbQnW73WJPQ3daS1k8biBaPb.jpg) Screenshot from [Vídeo](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/d-backs-vs-rockies/2026/02/20/831959/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
     Con el último bateador de ese episodio y el primero del siguiente (Braxton Fulford y Kyle Karros), los desafíos hechos en el último pitcheo de cada turno derivaron en el tercer strike, para ponchar a los peloteros quienes no le tiraron a los respectivos lanzamientos (habiendo sido cantados en \

). Y todo sucedió en los episodios 1 y 2, donde queda demostrado que el sistema ayudará a entregar juegos, con consecuencias más ajustadas a la realidad. El umpire de home, parecía que se enojaba con cada pedido de desafío, por lo cual imaginamos tendrá que ajustar su percepción de la zona en cada bateador. Si nos apegamos a la decisión de usar el sistema en primavera, el acierto se deriva en un período de ajuste necesario, antes que el espectáculo comience. Así las cosas, ya no se tratará de la culpa del \

dada la disponibilidad de la herramienta, sino que la responsabilidad recaerá en los protagonistas del juego: los peloteros. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     With the last batter of that inning and the first of the next (Braxton Fulford and Kyle Karros), challenges on the final pitch of each at-bat resulted in strikeouts, striking out the players who didn't swing at the pitches (which were called balls). This all happened in innings 1 and 2, demonstrating that the system will help deliver games with more realistic consequences. The home plate umpire seemed to get annoyed with each challenge, so we imagine he'll have to adjust his perception of the strike zone for each batter. If we stick to the decision to use the system in spring training, the success lies in a necessary adjustment period before the season begins. Therefore, the blame will no longer fall on the umpire, given the availability of the tool, but rather on the players themselves.

---

![Arenado.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/23xVEr8CuKJ2pxNejcrscikL32cDdm32fXXcxgVowAsjWj6ukJysGQpJvx1RD5En2P5DG.jpg) Screenshot from [Vídeo](https://www.mlb.com/es/gameday/d-backs-vs-rockies/2026/02/20/831959/final/video) --- # ![Firma Fermionico_Mesa de trabajo 1616.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/fermionico/QnCF6Qc3-Firma20Fermionico_Mesa20de20trabajo2016-16.png)
     Y fíjense si el sistema ayuda ajustar la zona, que los desafíos amainaron a partir del cuarto episodio, donde los catchers de ambos equipos no volvieron a pedir revisión. Antonio Senzatela fue limitado a dos episodios, tal como se acostumbra con los abridores a inicios de la primavera. Aceptó dos imparables (un jonrón de Nolan Arenado en la propia apertura del juego), dejando el partido 1-0. Al final, los DiamondBacks de Arizona se impusieron 3 carreras a 2, sobre los Rockies de Colorado, en una tarde de sol intenso ¿Qué más nos depara la primavera? Bueno, les recomiendo encarecidamente, aprovechen la oportunidad de ver juegos en MLB.tv anunciados como gratis. Será por un período corto de tiempo y vale la pena ver el sistema en acción, tal como a los futuros protagonistas del juego, quienes reciben muchos chances de jugar por éstos días. Los prospectos salen al campo a ganarse un puesto y se puede ver béisbol de calidad. También podrá ver \

, como el partido de ayer entre la North Eastern University y los Medias Rojas de Boston, el cual terminó con pizarra de 18-3 en 7 episodios. #
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

     And just look how much the system helps adjust the zone, because the challenges subsided starting in the fourth inning, with catchers from both teams not requesting another review. Antonio Senzatela was limited to two innings, as is customary for starting pitchers in early spring. He allowed two hits (a home run by Nolan Arenado in the very first inning), leaving the game 1-0. In the end, the Arizona Diamondbacks defeated the Colorado Rockies 3-2 on a sunny afternoon. What else does spring have in store for us? Well, I highly recommend taking advantage of the opportunity to watch games on MLB.tv advertised as free. It will be for a short period of time, and it's worth seeing the system in action, as well as the future stars of the game, who are getting plenty of chances to play these days. The prospects take the field to earn a spot, and you can see some quality baseball. You can also watch \

such as yesterday's game between North Eastern University and the Boston Red Sox, which ended with a score of 18-3 in 7 innings.

body.title: The Great Shrink
body.body:
# Why the Yen and Rural Japan are in decline?

Today, we’re talking about the Japanese Yen (JPY) and the demographic cliff Japan is currently base-jumping off of—without a parachute. In fact this conversation started as a discord message in the SL chat randomly. Since I have been studying this topic quite a bit I was able to supply quite a few plots quickly that surprised many people including a few Japanese individuals. If you’ve been following the news in 2025 and early 2026, you know the Yen has been acting like it’s allergic to value. But here’s the kicker: it’s not just about interest rates or trade deficits. It’s about the fact that there are simply fewer humans in Japan every single morning.


![Japan_popu_decline.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/48FE3idswFw69fr3EmC7qgzdrNBPvMW22gWwuZgTpkTg33j89Q336n68ApPzMc1DSV.png)

When a country loses 900,000 people in a single year, it loses consumers. Fewer consumers means companies stop investing locally and move their cash elsewhere. When the cash leaves, the Yen follows it out the door. It is that simple, and therefore, the correlation is that high!

# Rural Japan

While Tokyo still feels like a neon-soaked sardines-in-a-can situation, the rest of the country is quietly vanishing. We aren't just talking about a \

In rural prefectures like Akita, the population is dropping by nearly 2% every single year.\n\nThe magnitude of the decline in the countryside is staggering compared to the national average. We have roughly 9 million abandoned houses (Akiya) across the country. In villages like [Nanmoku](https://maps.app.goo.gl/r8fTQpzw7hoNaNkYA), only 2 hrs by car from Tokyo Shinjuku station, over 67% of the residents are over 65. When the labor force disappears, the economy doesn't just \

—it evaporates.


![Rural_Prefectures.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/23t77B89nSgjLAmtmzxFkTgqhXtS49gnmKnvUKfecEcXxPnByNCjti6dKAfJ8L8HFBVW1.png)

As the rural areas hollow out, the tax base craters. To keep the lights on, the government has to print, borrow, and pray. This structural weakness puts a permanent \

on the Yen. In the last 10 years, the correlation between the population growth rate and the JPY value has sat at a staggering 0.87.

The data tells a stark story: while Japan’s national population decline has accelerated into the -0.65% range, the situation in rural Japan is far more dramatic. In prefectures like Akita, the population is shrinking at more than three times the national rate, hitting -2.0% annually by 2024.

# The \
Leaderboard (2025-2026 Data)\n\nThe northern Tōhoku region, where I travelled quite a bit recently, is essentially the \

of this crisis. Here are the prefectures seeing the sharpest drops in their native populations:

| Prefecture | Annual Decline Rate (%) | Key Characteristic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Akita** | **-1.91%** | Highest elderly ratio (over 40% are 65+) |
| **Aomori** | **-1.72%** | Massive youth out-migration to Tokyo |
| **Kōchi** | **-1.71%** | Sharpest decline in the Shikoku region |
| **Iwate** | **-1.69%** | Significant rural hollowing out |

I’d call Akita the \
—essentially deciding which ghost towns to stop providing water and electricity to.\n\n# The \

Index: Akiya

In Japan, there is a name for these abandoned houses: Akiya (空き家). As of 2024, there are roughly 9 million of them. That is nearly 14% of all homes in the country sitting empty, slowly being reclaimed by the mountain forests. There are numerous videos on YouTube where people are 'buying' free houses from the government. Here is one in the Seto In-land Sea area...

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=08t2yB6ApKA&t=446s

In a normal economy, a house is an asset. In rural Japan, an Akiya is a liability.

- The Valuation Trap: In places like Akita or Aomori, you can buy a house for the price of a used Toyota—or sometimes literally 1 Yen. But nobody wants them because the cost of demolition ($10,000 to $30,000) is higher than the value of the land.

- The Tax Black Hole: When a homeowner dies and the children have already fled to Tokyo, they often refuse the inheritance to avoid the property taxes. This leaves the municipality with a \

property that generates zero tax revenue but still requires maintenance.\n\nThere is a poetic, yet tragic, correlation between the Akiya rate and the JPY value. As the number of empty houses climbs toward a projected 30% by 2033, the structural \
on the Japanese economy grows.\n\nInvestors look at a country where 1 out of every 3 buildings might soon be a ruin and they ask: \

the capital leaves, and the Yen drops.

So, bottomline, if you want to travel to Japan, which is spectacular, go now. Prices are cheap, and likely will remain cheap for a while.

body.title: Beautifully Toned Silver Mexican Golden Eagle Coin
body.body: \nThis past week I mentioned that I have been feeling a little under the weather. I am feeling quite a bit better, still a little lower on energy than I would like. Then again, I would love to have the energy I had when I was 21, but I'll conform myself with a return to my current \

... While I was down I was sifting through some files on an old laptop, backing up old family photos and those of my son. In the process I found an old file with some pictures of some silver items, and I shared one recently.

Today I have   another pick out of the file.  I have always been a big fan of Mexican coinage and have been collecting it ever since I lived in Arizona. This was the early 2000's and silver prices were cheap, so I gladly snapped  up any good deals I could find. Out of some of those I must have picked up this one as well.

What catches my eye about this one in particular is the toning on the obverse (front) of the coin. It really draws out so much more detail that you can't easily see with a pristine, white shiny background. It almost makes the golden eagle looks a little \

!






https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcSHkUiTpuxBCP8cNwYotYjpgebE4EXpPJY6fC69uASG8/Screenshot%204673.png 
 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVx3toNKzRyz9rLFcK1xUArDggNzMsuAPZrUsqrW2ChHw/Screenshot%204675.png 

 
 ## **About the coin**:




 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmTEPcdYy83FQdAsaQX6dvoEDLVCBrCy4hivN4iotcBR18/Screenshot%204677.png 
From numista.com

What I love about these 5 Pesos coins is they contain a lot of silver and are pretty hefty. They also have the beautiful imagery created by the Mexico City Mint, which is the oldest mint in the Americas. The obverse has the golden eagle with a rattlesnake it's caught as prey perched atop a prickly pear cactus.  It's become an iconic image for any Mexican coin fan.  The reverse (back) of the coin has  Cuauhtémoc an ancient Aztec leader that  led his people after the Spanish had invaded. The conquistador Hernán Cortés hanged him fearing an uprising, but in the process made him a martyr that is still respected in Mexico today.

This coin in addition to the great patina has 0.868 Troy ounces of silver, worth about $73.50 at the time of writing. However, collectors will pay considerably more depending on the coin's condition. I won't be selling any time soon however, I like my Mexican silver!




 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUQzYAmvgifAX8Xc7RZ4bmxjEvrJA6PT2T92XvrSt2Qvv/image.png 

## **Silver**

Silver prices have been up again with the current world instability concerning Iran and the world economy. Over the last five days prices have risen $10 per Troy ounce, which brings into the question is this going to be a sustainable trend in the long run? After the last quick run up we saw a huge crash, hopefully we aren't in for the same kind of surprise all over again! 

Silver is still in short supply that will likely push prices higher, and eastern exchanges have also been pressing those prices upward. Just look at the chart over the last five days:


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYvekbLkUQsxbrK5DBpQ5fGMmiMM3zrMZZE1wBHYarRWx/Screenshot%204678.png 
From kitco.com

It's always a good idea to invest in precious metals, they will always have value no matter what happens in the world. Just remember the rule of thumb, if you don't physically possess the precious metal it isn't really yours. Just like BTC and Hive!






 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmay1VYGkPJEY33bsAi1nuUzULQm6S8t8TyP1hRRzVVmaX/image.png 

That will do it for this Saturday, I hope you enjoyed seeing the nice Mexican silver coin, they always produce such nice work! Please feel free to leave any comments or questions below, and thanks for all of your support. It's greatly appreciated! Have a great weekend everyone!

body.title: Manejo de la biomasa del bosque secundario
body.body:
*..Aprende a escuchar el renacimiento de un bosque...*

A veces, la naturaleza solo necesita que nos quitemos de en medio. Un bosque secundario,ese que surge después de un incendio, una tala o el abandono de un potrero, es en esencia, la Tierra intentando curarse a sí misma.

Muchos ven \

donde en realidad hay una voluntad inmensa de vivir. Manejar su biomasa no se trata de dominarlo, sino de acompañarlo en su camino de regreso a la plenitud.

#### Devolver antes que quitar.

En la cultura del \

, solemos querer limpiar el suelo. Pero en el bosque, el desorden es vida. Cada rama caída y cada hoja seca es un aporte de amor al suelo. Al dejar que la biomasa se descomponga en el sitio, estamos permitiendo que el bosque se alimente de su propio pasado. No es basura; es el abono más puro que existe. Ayudar al que tiene sed de luz.\n\nImagina que eres un joven Cedro rodeado de arbustos que no te dejan ver el sol. Aquí es donde nuestra mano entra: podemos ayudar a esos árboles \

despejando un poco su entorno. No es una limpieza radical, es un abrazo de luz. Quitamos un poco de presión para que la vida más fuerte pueda alcanzar el cielo. Bosque del Bobito : ![16491.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVKPomyNGVnKGj4AnFVcNfjMqgAcJta9wypnNNx3aTwet/16491.jpg) ![16492.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYLeAdtU5bePgZzrUQX1HmtrQr1ZMxG6zHUho7jhupLgF/16492.jpg) #### El silencio de la madera muerta tiene una belleza profunda, como un tronco que se deshace. En la ecología del corazón, entendemos que un árbol caído sigue trabajando: da refugio al escarabajo, alimento al hongo y humedad a la semilla que apenas despierta. Manejar la biomasa con sentido humano es respetar el ciclo del fin, entendiendo que nada se pierde, todo se transforma. Es un acto de paciencia. Manejar un bosque secundario es un ejercicio de humildad. Es entender que no somos los dueños del paisaje, sino sus guardianes. Cada gramo de biomasa que protegemos es aire limpio para nuestros hijos y un hogar recuperado para las aves que habían olvidado el camino a casa. Perspectiva de la pendiente : ![16497.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRofCJPw3UigXomNQ8ZAwBg9wxURZL42LNaGS8m9KgyQ6/16497.jpg) ![16498.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW4boLKgbQaApiq1Jc3MGUdKKYmJgBCzyJMAC11H1xQ7o/16498.jpg) Manejo de la biomasa ![16499.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmayDc7JhmsHeDXDS55TPqQKFSCjhug3Zod3QGbFtPWjhz/16499.jpg) ![16500.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdzttkBSrv7x9YB6847HhSXrdmsjG8TyuGV124VBsH18x/16500.jpg)

body.title: HATING THE PROCESS
body.body: If you ask me whether I love my job right now, my answer will be a big fat YES. I love the thrill and drill it provides. It keeps me busy wondering what I am doing right or wrong and pushes me to be better at my job. But 6 months ago, this wasn’t the case, I was so frustrated with everything going on around me that I allowed myself to sink into despair, then came the realization that with all my years of working, a new admin personnel earns my salary in her probationary period. To be honest I was angry because I could not understand how the hell the HR would do that to me. Then I realized all the staffs due for raise have all gotten except me. I know because I control the company server and am in charge of every mail coming in and out of the server. At first I thought if I was patient mine would come but after about two months I realized the company was not going to give me a raise.\n\n

/> This made my morale drop, it was clear that there was clearly politics going on and when I went to the HR for answers she admitted my name was submitted for a raise but because the new admin is very close to my MDs wife, my name was removed in order to balance the company's account. The HR is a very good friend of mine, and from how she spoke it was clear that she had tried everything to revert it, but it was now beyond her knowing the order came from my MDs wife. At that point I was really disappointed, it felt a system I was working so hard for did not even regard me in the slightest. With that I started looking for a new Job and I got one which offered me more than my current salary but it officially took my weekends. While I was considering this new Job, my MD suddenly called me alongside the HR and consultant. He called because he noticed the drop in my work rate and wanted to know what was happening. I held nothing back explaining my displeasure as I felt my efforts were not being noticed. This was what brought the whole truth out, He addressed it and now things are better. Turned out the new admin could not handle the pressure in oil and gas and decided to resign, so much for sidelining me lol. ##### PICTURE CREDIT IS MINE

body.title: Hope on one side, hesitation on the other.🌄💙🐱💛🐈
body.body: Greetings lovely members of the community. I hope you all are doing great and enjoying quality time with your loved ones. > समुदाय के प्यारे सदस्यों को नमस्कार। मुझे आशा है कि आप सभी अच्छे होंगे और अपने प्रियजनों के साथ गुणवत्तापूर्ण समय का आनंद ले रहे है। ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRpkUCUHDf3zntZ44ceX1MSqHCGCiufubGGfWngv3chci/1771691703223.jpg) Yesterday at sunset, the new cat was back on the balcony again. The light was soft and golden, and both of them were sitting there quietly. >कल शाम सूरज ढलते समय नया बिल्ली फिर से बालकनी में आया हुआ था। हल्की सुनहरी रोशनी फैली हुई थी और दोनों चुपचाप बैठे थे। ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRXBgFJWrrwYrX3TN1PkcZ3f2eJbr7qz4K5aPATtangLg/1771691703735.jpg) The other cats haven’t really welcomed him properly from the start. There’s always been a bit of distance. This time, the little kitten tried to get closer to him. He walked up slowly, curious and hopeful, just trying to get familiar. >शुरू से ही बाकी बिल्लियों ने उसे ठीक से स्वीकार नहीं किया है। हमेशा उनके बीच थोड़ा सा फासला रहा है। इस बार छोटा बिल्ली का बच्चा उसके पास जाने की कोशिश कर रहा था। वह धीरे-धीरे, जिज्ञासा और उम्मीद के साथ उसके करीब आया, बस थोड़ा परिचित होना चाहता था। ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY8GPBnsrZTWpQLZn6hLSaaEVYFaMShgmKVs6xTmFbaP1/1771691704235.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYdSEd5WMzVDBJ5SbKmrQYTN9rT9btwpgXzGHbGBkT96B/1771691705021.jpg) But as soon as the kitten came near, the new cat hissed at him. It wasn’t a big fight, just a clear refusal. It felt like he wasn’t interested in bonding at all. Maybe he just comes for the food and leaves. body.body:
>

Hello good people on hive...


Some time ago, I received a photo from a friend of mine—one I met through a writing community. She had originally asked my permission to share one of my books with junior high school students, where she would be teaching writing, like a workshop. I naturally agreed, and she later sent me these photos.

![FB_IMG_1761031258709.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/viviehardika/23w2nsZ1rHgtCv2c5rxMe59GKTMugHt7E2tHDj1qyFYPLcQoMaoxY51BHb9vzsY8UmvmN.jpg)

![FB_IMG_1761031253225.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/viviehardika/23vhwxccChQG8w2iUsLYzEQ1vWPFPmP5NpToMrwQxDPfzzoHhJLvEZdBLXQ3RWMXbfbnQ.jpg)

Seeing it reminded me of a few years ago when I self-published that book on impulse. Then, because it wasn't very popular, my books ended up back in storage, and I immediately adopted them. It didn't stop there. Due to the rental's poor humidity, some of the books were eaten by termites and damaged. Eventually, I had to give away the new books to fellow writers and share them.

So that's why this book ended up in the hands of these children. I hope it can help them with literacy and achieve their dreams. I hope so...


Anyway... Hasta La Vista...

-------

*See you on the next post...*

body.title: Stunned as if hit on the head with a hammer
body.body:
While my colleague was telling me about pubs in Novi Sad that, in addition to excellent beers, also have good food, a [visit to the city pub](https://ecency.com/hive-187719/@duskobgd/beer-sausages-and-a-bit) in Novi Sad a year and a half ago was running through my mind...

HOG Pub, which he told me about, pours beers that are produced in a craft brewery in Novi Sad and they have several beers on offer.
\
.\nI made the decision to stop by the moment he told me: \

.

Due to the January and February celebrations I have every year, and the amount of alcohol I drank during those celebrations, I didn't get to taste the beers I would feature on #beersaturday but this Saturday, I'm off duty, I don't need to drive anywhere, so I'll treat myself to a good beer.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbyTiwDGeyyJHs8CoWRk9da7wxU8WQBoPyHcvyXJu1PFP/1771666004771.jpg)

I stopped by the HOG pub ​​in the morning.
The pub had just opened, so the bartender and the waitress looked at me in amazement, probably thinking \

😀

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZgJtQLmdbdnR99fVGvkWQwfitwQfSjQ8LEU96N9hGvgX/1771666054573.jpg)

I asked the bartender to give me bottles of all the beers they have on tap, to see which one I would choose and after analyzing the labels, I decided on Mjolnir, NOT IPA style.
Thor, I've already drunk Classic IPA, but NOT IPA was the winner for me between:
Loki, Amber Ale
Ragnar, American Pale Ale
Bjorn, German Wheat Ale
Freyja, American blonde Ale

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaZ64xSqHPNU5aVzdAGUqtCUShP83uWmpxykfLp2NugxL/1771666054790.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTmpS3CjCXzaXFfxF2mCc1GscvrxV2daRnzZMQ7CJNmYt/1771666177244.jpg)

The waiter poured me a liter and I hurried home, to park the car and taste Mjolnir.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNYX6NGTteewG65NjBiC4qsdttcZxgssgY6iDPj335P4q/1771666240493.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPGZYCoTo5uJEqdHRAVZvvhp8GgRNgSasaKTPBg1ecJ8A/1771666240902.jpg)

**Hummer of God**
***Mjolnir***
NewEngland IPA special unfiltered, unpasteurized, cloudy beer, in addition to water, it contains barley and wheat malt, oat and wheat flakes, hops and yeast.
As soon as I looked at the Mjolnar label, I knew what kind of beer was waiting for me.
With an extract of 15.3%, 6.4% alcohol is expected, with a full body and quite thick beer, and a high foam, which I believe, due to the citrus and tropical notes, will be drinkable.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdz3n5CpJJoeDFj1ZXrdav82U41qvRsVNp4jrAL41YnSh/1771666773536.jpg)

As soon as I opened the bottle into which my beer was poured, the beautiful smell of tropical fruits spread around me.
When pouring, it gives a very firm, persistent foam, two fingers thick.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWT7U4bavTJPke51CfJMK7CQoeGZoYwuFteFzTMJsUESS/1771666024178.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYftDbFgvdscGgh6G1Cr8okwdmzH8ARhso65fqPzA121Z/1771692366780.gif)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbWqKiM69LnXu7sQbpETfMRQdWMu2DUf7uzPudWmRLUzJ/1771666325819.jpg)

Before the first sip, I put my nose to the top of the glass and if I hadn't seen what I poured into the glass, I would have thought that there was a bowl of tropical fruit in front of me.
What a nice refreshing fruity scent.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUb8depg2zspDWPhFmwpeD9knuajL6HhpCDkoqhh5iopB/1771666326012.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYj9uG7KkbKnvgQr51uQ2UszsZ3tzCxMrgUyFYPkckNpP/1771666414635.jpg)

The first sip, the refreshing aromas of citrus, on my tongue completely eliminated any feeling of a higher percentage of alcohol, and the taste of fruit remained the entire time of drinking the beer.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVyBTWPXBGUDxqa5PqRLaBpZZuWn9wk9vxg3dLqdevy6T/1771666448773.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTUtpfppq3TiQmpiaFghmhD8SWG3RTQnxugt8PunyXwXi/1771666448967.jpg)
The HOG brawery stated for this beer:
\

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY9Gz8MHA8gZFbWCYgV8RoWdt3dqRy9jRWbibXkjKTvsN/1771666449142.jpg)

I agree with every line of this text.
It's just that this hammer Tora knocked me down and got me really drunk 🙂
They say \

orange grapefruit color?
Is it possible that I am in a daze because of such a beautiful color? I don't think so and that the 6.4% alcohol content of this beer had an effect on the stupor.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX7NCiZmUs3o2PYBtU3NRakgExmXukaYpMNUqNePwYNqp/1771666449321.jpg)

While I'm sitting and drinking the last sips of this great beer, I'm already making a combination in my head of how to get to the HOG Pub without a car, and to try the other beers of the HOG brewery directly on the taps.
Because, if out of the 6 they have on offer, I can recommend two, I definitely think that I should give the remaining wheat, lager and red beers a chance, and at the same time enjoy the fantastic food that my colleague told me about.
Until then, I welcome you with one **Cheers** and have a nice weekend.

body.title: I Should Have Read It First, Roald Dahl’s Henry Sugar
body.body:
I watched The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar on Netflix mainly because Wes Anderson made it. It was 39 minutes long, which felt about right. The sets looked like dioramas, the narration moved fast, and Benedict Cumberbatch played Henry like someone who was used to getting what he wanted. I liked it a lot.

But when it was over, I kept thinking: I should have read the story first.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUXCxac3CWXyXCFo6uZAGRY2LaitmHeqhJb7JKAY7jCUC/img_1567.png)
[img source](https://perpustakaan.jakarta.go.id/book/detail?cn=JAKPU-12139000001263)

Going back to Roald Dahl’s original, I was struck by how good the writing was. Simple, direct, no extra weight. He did not waste words but he also did not rush. The story went in layers, a report inside a story inside a life, and on screen that felt clever, but on the page I sat with it longer. The whole thing had more room to settle.

What I did not expect was that the story was really about two people, not one. Henry got the title, but the man who trained for years until he could see without his eyes was the one I kept thinking about. In Dahl original, he was called Imhrat Khan, played in the film by Ben Kingsley under the name Imdad Khan. Nobody seemed to know why Anderson changed it. His part of the story felt quieter and stranger than the rest, and it made Henry change feel earned.

The Imhrat Khan section was almost entirely dialogue. A doctor asking questions, a man answering them, back and forth, page after page. On paper that sounds like it should drag. It did not. Dahl wrote it in a way that kept pulling forward, each answer leading to a stranger question, each explanation opening up something that did not quite make sense until suddenly it did. I read that section twice. The second time I noticed I was hearing Ben Kingsley voice the whole way through, very calm, very deliberate, with that slight pause before each sentence. I could not unhear it. And then somewhere in the middle I started seeing Richard Ayoade sitting cross legged on the floor as the yogi, which made the whole thing funnier than it was probably meant to be. Dahl wrote the yogi as this ancient, deeply serious figure. Ayoade is a deeply funny person just by existing. Those two things do not fully go together and now I cannot separate them.

Going between the book and the film, small differences started adding up. In Dahl original, the doctor who recorded the whole thing was a British surgeon named John Cartwright. Anderson replaced him with Dr. Chatterjee, played by Dev Patel, a South Asian doctor. It was not a dramatic change but it was a deliberate one. Dahl original text had a colonial feel to it and Anderson quietly removed that. The yogi in the book had a name too, Banerjee. In the film, Richard Ayoade played him but the name was gone. And then there was Ralph Fiennes as Dahl himself, appearing as a narrator from the very beginning. In the original, Dahl only showed up at the very end. Anderson moved him to the front and built the whole frame around him.

The book also spent more time showing just how self-absorbed Henry was before his change. Dahl wrote about his capped yellow teeth, a mole he had removed by a plastic surgeon, a hand cream he used made from turtle oil. Small details, but they added up to a portrait of a man who was completely consumed by himself. The film skipped most of that. It moved too fast to linger.

I also went in expecting a twist. Dahl was known for those. It never came. Instead the story did something harder: it took a greedy, bored man, put him through years of real work, and let him become someone different. No big moment, no speech. It just happened. That was hard to write, and Dahl made it look easy.

The film stayed close to the text, almost word for word in places. Some critics called it a glorified audiobook and I understood that. It moved fast and kept its distance. Reading the story after watching filled in what the film left just out of reach.

If I did it again, I would read first, then watch. The film was good, good enough to win an Oscar. But the writing, the sentences, the pace, the way Dahl made something strange feel normal, that was the better part.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

body.title: Your Journey Begins the Moment You Decide
body.body:
Hello everyone,
how are you all? I hope everyone is fine and doing great in their life.

There is a saying that it is never too late to start something, or that it is better late than never. If you are someone who is afraid to start just because it feels like you are already late, then you are not alone. It is actually very normal to think that way.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZhvQgaFwvnEHFdD7B3SSemdUe8kEGi91MhzhYbsCaC1F/image.png)

<a href=\

>Source Many people go through a phase where they feel they should have started something much earlier than they are starting now. One good example can be seen in many top-level brands where the founders actually started building their businesses after the age of 30. So even if you are in your 20s, it is not late at all to start something. You just need to get on the right path, build the right skills, learn the right things, and enter the right sector to find a meaningful role for yourself in the industry. No matter when you completed your degree, skills are something that can be developed at any time. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZiUPuqxpsSraXHYkmKVGpzT24cZ4NRiwy3xxVCSFN8vW/image.png)

>Source If you are going through this situation, calm down and just start. Do not overthink about being late, about not succeeding, or about giving up before even trying. These thoughts will keep running in your mind, but you have to move past them. Remember, you have nothing to lose. Just start and see where you land. At the end of the day, you will become a better person by trying and beginning your journey than by giving up without even taking the first step. --- This section is for the games I play on Hive blockchain. body.title: One of my favorite Videogame Sagas is now dead.  - Saints Row
body.body:
Gracias por pasar, version en español abajo
https://img.somosxbox.com/somosxbox/2020/04/22053539/saints-row-2019.jpg

---

Today we're going to talk about my past, yes. Something a little different from the posts I usually write, but I've found out that one of my favorite series has been relegated to the drawer of forgotten games, and I think that's the only thing left to do, considering everything that's happened to it.

I remember when talking about Saints Row meant talking about fun chaos. It wasn't GTA, and that's precisely why it was so appealing. It was more exaggerated, more ridiculous, more cheeky. It didn't take itself too seriously, and that was part of its charm. It gave you an open city and told you \

but with a crooked smile.

---

https://generacionxbox.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/saints-row-min.jpg

---

When Saints Row 2 came out, many of us felt that the series had found its identity. It had a story, it had absurd moments, but it also knew when to get serious. Then came Saints Row: The Third, and that was like hitting the gas pedal without looking back. More explosions, more craziness, more personality. It was impossible not to have fun. The series understood that it couldn't compete directly with GTA in realism, so it decided to compete in spectacle.

---

https://fanatical.imgix.net/product/original/6e880ca2-5f48-43e7-ad6b-81ec08bd57a4.jpg?auto=compress,format&w=872&fit=crop&h=491

---

Then came Saints Row IV, and that's when something strange started. Yes, it was fun. Yes, flying around the city with superpowers had its charm. But you were no longer a criminal building an empire; you were basically a superhero fighting aliens in a simulation. It was entertaining, but it also felt like the series was running away from itself. Like it didn't know how to evolve without becoming a complete caricature.

---

https://www.muycomputer.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Saints-Row-1.jpg

---

Then came Agents of Mayhem. It wasn't exactly Saints Row, but it was connected in spirit and design. And that's where the wear and tear was already showing. It didn't make a big impact, it didn't generate lasting conversation, it didn't leave a mark. It was one of those games that comes out, a few people try it, and a month later nobody's talking about it anymore.

And then came the 2022 reboot, Saints Row. It was supposed to be the rebirth. The moment to say, \

But what came out was something that didn't convince either old or new fans. The characters lacked their charisma. The tone tried to be modern, but it felt forced. The humor was no longer irreverent; it was just bizarre. And technically, it didn't help either: bugs, a generic feel, and unsurprising missions.

---

https://prod-images.blacknut.net/61ea9d349233172d29e01a05_hd.jpg

---

The worst part wasn't that it was terrible. It was that it was mediocre. And mediocrity kills faster than disaster—something that's become clear to me after watching recent releases. A bad game can become a cult classic. A lukewarm one is simply forgotten.

---

https://i0.wp.com/brainstomping.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/saints-row-3.jpg?ssl=1

---

Sales obviously weren't what was expected, and that had real consequences. The studio behind the saga, Volition, ended up closing. Thirty years of history vanished with a corporate decision. And when the studio that created the DNA of a franchise disappears, it's not just an administrative closure; it's a symbolic blow. It's as if they were officially telling you, \

--- https://poluxweb.com/Polux3/images/data/videojuegos/2022/septiembre/Resenas/SaintsRow/Saints-row-11.jpg --- In practice, it's dead now, yes. There are no announcements, no clear plans, no signs that anyone is working on bringing it back to life. And even if someone buys the IP tomorrow and announces another game, it won't be the same. Because the problem wasn't just a bad launch; it was a complete disconnect from what made the series special. That's it. I wanted to share a piece of my history as a gamer. I think this is one of the series I've enjoyed the most, even more than GTA at times, so here it is, and I personally recommend the fourth game.
![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/pP0zwWZoqv4AAAAC/saints-row-iv-saints-row.gif)






### Español
https://img.somosxbox.com/somosxbox/2020/04/22053539/saints-row-2019.jpg --- Hoy vamos a hablar de mi pasado, si. algo un poco diferente a los post que suelo hacer pero es que me he enterado que una de mis sagas favoritas ha sido puesta en el cajon de los juegos olvidados, y creo que es lo unico que faltaba por hacer viendo todo lo que ha pasado con ella Yo recuerdo cuando hablar de Saints Row era hablar de caos divertido. No era GTA, y justamente por eso gustaba. Era más exagerado, más ridículo, más descarado. No se tomaba demasiado en serio y eso era parte de su encanto. Te daba una ciudad abierta y te decía “haz lo que quieras”, pero con una sonrisa torcida. --- https://generacionxbox.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/saints-row-min.jpg --- Cuando salió Saints Row 2 muchos sentimos que ahí la saga encontró su identidad. Tenía historia, tenía momentos absurdos, pero también sabía ponerse serio cuando hacía falta. Después vino Saints Row: The Third y eso fue como pisar el acelerador sin mirar atrás. Más explosiones, más locura, más personalidad. Era imposible no divertirse. La saga entendía que no podía competir directamente con GTA en realismo, así que decidió competir en espectáculo. --- https://fanatical.imgix.net/product/original/6e880ca2-5f48-43e7-ad6b-81ec08bd57a4.jpg?auto=compress,format&w=872&fit=crop&h=491 --- Luego llegó Saints Row IV y ahí empezó algo raro. Sí, era divertido. Sí, volar por la ciudad con superpoderes tenía su gracia. Pero ya no eras un criminal construyendo un imperio, eras básicamente un superhéroe peleando contra alienígenas en una simulación. Era entretenido, pero también se sentía como si la saga estuviera huyendo de sí misma. Como si no supiera cómo evolucionar sin volverse completamente caricatura. --- https://www.muycomputer.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Saints-Row-1.jpg --- Después vino Agents of Mayhem. No era exactamente Saints Row, pero estaba conectado en espíritu y estudio. Y ahí ya se notaba el desgaste. No pegó fuerte, no generó conversación duradera, no dejó huella. Fue uno de esos juegos que salen, algunos lo prueban, y al mes ya nadie habla de él. Y entonces llegó el reboot de 2022, Saints Row. Se suponía que era el renacer. El momento de decir “ok, aprendimos, volvemos con algo fresco pero fiel”. Pero lo que salió fue algo que no convenció ni a los fans viejos ni a los nuevos. Los personajes no tenían el mismo carisma. El tono intentaba ser moderno, pero se sentía forzado. El humor ya no era irreverente, era extraño. Y técnicamente tampoco ayudó: bugs, sensación de juego genérico, misiones que no sorprendían. --- https://prod-images.blacknut.net/61ea9d349233172d29e01a05_hd.jpg --- Lo peor no fue que fuera terrible. Fue que fue mediocre. Y la mediocridad mata más rápido que el desastre eso es algo que me ha quedado claro viendo lanzamientos recientes. Un juego malo puede volverse de culto. Uno tibio simplemente se olvida. --- https://i0.wp.com/brainstomping.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/saints-row-3.jpg?ssl=1 --- Las ventas obviamente no fueron lo que se esperaba y eso tuvo consecuencias reales. El estudio detrás de la saga, Volition, terminó cerrando. Treinta años de historia se fueron con una decisión corporativa. Y cuando el estudio que creó el ADN de una franquicia desaparece, no es solo un cierre administrativo, es un golpe simbólico. Es como si te dijeran oficialmente “esto ya no tiene futuro”. --- https://poluxweb.com/Polux3/images/data/videojuegos/2022/septiembre/Resenas/SaintsRow/Saints-row-11.jpg --- En la práctica está muerto ahora, sí. No hay anuncios, no hay planes claros, no hay señales de que alguien esté trabajando en devolverlo a la vida. Y aunque mañana alguien compre la IP y anuncie otro juego, ya no sería lo mismo. Porque el problema no fue solo un mal lanzamiento, fue una desconexión total con lo que hacía especial a la saga. Ya está, queria publicar un pedazo de mi historia como videojugador, creo que esta es una de las sagas que mas disfrute incluso por momentos mas que los GTA asi que aqui se los dejo y les dejo como recomendacion personal el cuarto juego

body.title: Antelope turns the tables on a Leopard
body.body:
This is the most unexpected video I've ever seen in my lifetime. I already know some animals considered can get aggressive but not in a million years did I expect an antelope to dominate a leopard to this degree. 

https://youtube.com/shorts/6Mz65A9HoC0?si=vv88lUmdaL-p9bXF

Perhaps I've not been watching all the animal documentary video but the leopard had its ass kicked by an antelope which is supposed to be prey.

If you look at the antelope body structure, it's reasonable to say it has parts that can be used to fight. An antelope has horns, it has legs that can break a ribcage. These are facts about an animal we file under prey.

Lions and leopards and almost all wild big cats gets all the language of power. The antelope gets described in relation to the wild cat family as in what it provides, what it runs from. The whole vocabulary around it is about absence. Speed as the absence of confrontation, survival as the act of not being eaten. It's the way we see preys.

Now I'm looking at a cornered antelope brutally beat up a leopard, why shouldn't I be surprised?

But whether you're a beast or not, you can be vulnerable at times. A predator still has to calculate. A broken leg in the wild is a slow end. So even a wild beasts pause and assess situations because a mistake can lead to a disgraceful YouTube video about them.

Even a lions the kings of the jungle or I would prefer to say savannah, reads the situation. The antelope with nowhere to go is a different proposition from the antelope in open field. The leopard knows this, we are the ones who forget it.

There is a cost to pressing anything into a corner. That cost is real whether or not the thing being cornered looks dangerous at first. If the prey chooses fight instead of flight, the predator stands a chance of being cooked.

If you're also surprised, it's probably because the label, prey, does a lot of work. It becomes a total description. It looks like a permanent condition. But it was always just an ecological role, a position in a system and the animal inside that role has been shaped by millions of years of exactly the same pressures as the predator. The same arms race. The hooves are part of it, the horns are part of it. It'll evolve to survive.

body.body:
1/2 🧵 The Ibanez Tube Screamer TS9 is a legendary overdrive pedal that's been a staple in guitar rigs since 1982. It's famous for its warm, mid-focused overdrive that doesn't completely obliterate your original tone — instead, it compresses and smooths out the signal while adding harmonic richness.

The TS9 uses a JRC4558D op-amp chip (in original versions) and has three simple controls: Drive, Tone, and Level. The magic is in how it sculpts the midrange — it cuts bass slightly and boosts mids around 720Hz, which helps guitar solos cut through a dense mix without getting shrill.

Stevie Ray Vaughan made it iconic, but it's been used by everyone from Gary Moore to John Mayer to The Edge. Players often stack it into already-driven amps to tighten low end and add sustain, rather than using it as their only source of gain.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
2/2 🧵 The TS9 differs from the earlier TS808 mainly in the output section and slightly different filtering — the 808 is considered warmer and smoother, while the TS9 has a bit more edge. Tons of boutique clones exist (Fulltone OCD, Maxon OD808, JHS Bonsai) because the circuit is relatively simple but incredibly effective.

If you're looking at one, the reissue models are solid, but vintage units from the '80s command premium prices. For most players, a modern TS9 or even a TS Mini gets you 90% of the way there at a fraction of the cost.

body.title: My Favourite Athlete – Not Just a Winner, But a Reminder
body.body:
Hello @everyone, greetings to all from @theindicators. How are you feeling today I hope all are fine and I'm also good 👍 😊.
Today's I wants to share a childhood memories 
Sometimes I think we don’t realise the value of someone until they make the whole country pause.
The first time I seriously noticed Arshad Nadeem was not even during a live match. I was scrolling on my phone. Internet slow, as usual. Someone had shared his throw clip.
I clicked it casually.
But when that javelin left his hand… I don’t know why, I sat straight.
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmWstnSSjcnUfcHsEvyBFNu3RPDvBDCiYu4gzGJxHVpaP2/grok_image_1771690953966.jpg 


It wasn’t just distance. It was confidence.
I remember when I was in school, we had a sports day. I once tried javelin with a bamboo stick (not professional of course). I threw it so badly that my friends laughed for weeks. After that, I never tried again.
That’s the difference between people like me and athletes like him.
They don’t stop after one bad throw.
What makes Arshad Nadeem special for me is simple — he didn’t grow up with perfect facilities. No international-level grounds. No luxury training environment.
Still, he competed against the world.
And won.
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPQuHWNEKy8x4CTButAjGaRV3V92kRZNi7N4puV32KjMq/grok_image_1771691014769.jpg 


When he stood with the Pakistan flag, I actually felt goosebumps. It wasn’t just pride. It was relief. Like finally someone proved that talent from our soil is enough.
In my own life, I struggle with consistency. Some days I feel motivated. Some days I don’t even want to open my laptop. But when I see someone like him, I feel slightly embarrassed of my excuses.
He throws a javelin 80+ meters.
I can’t even throw away my laziness sometimes.
But maybe that’s why he is my favourite athlete.
Not because he is perfect.
But because he shows what discipline looks like.
He reminds me that background is not an excuse.
And maybe one day, if I stay consistent in my small field, I can also achieve something worth remembering.
Until then, I’ll keep watching, learning, and trying.
